classification.notes: Configuration-driven dispatch with Eval(), dynamic form name, dynamic callback. Cannot be statically analyzed. Migration requires understanding of the data in tblFormConfig at runtime, which the harvester cannot see.

resolvedCallee.notes: Eval() evaluates arbitrary VBA expressions at runtime. Content comes from a database table - can contain ANY valid VBA. No static analysis possible.

arguments.notes: Form name is a runtime String, not a compile-time identifier. Cannot determine which form is opened.

resolvedCallee.notes: Application.Run dispatches to a procedure by name string. Equivalent to reflection-based invocation. Target procedure cannot be determined statically.

unresolvedItems.context: Procedure evaluates arbitrary VBA expressions read from tblFormConfig.FilterTemplate. The expressions are stored as data, not code. Static analysis cannot determine what expressions will execute. Migration requires either: (a) preserving Eval() semantics with a runtime expression engine, (b) replacing config-driven Eval with structured config (e.g., predicate trees), or (c) inventorying actual values in tblFormConfig and translating each individually as a special case.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Recommended: extract all values currently stored in tblFormConfig.FilterTemplate, classify by pattern, and design typed replacements for each pattern class. Eval() does not have a clean migration path.

unresolvedItems.context: Form name is a runtime String value read from tblFormConfig.FormName. The harvester cannot determine which forms might be opened. Affects navigation graph, dependency analysis, and dead-code detection.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Inventory distinct values of tblFormConfig.FormName and treat each as a possible navigation target. Migration target should explicitly enumerate the supported form set rather than leaving form selection data-driven, OR maintain the data-driven dispatch with a typed registry pattern.

unresolvedItems.context: Procedure name is a runtime String read from tblFormConfig.Callback. Equivalent to reflection-based dispatch. Cannot determine which procedures might be invoked.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Inventory distinct values of tblFormConfig.Callback. If small set: replace with explicit dispatch (switch). If large or open-ended: migration target needs registry pattern or rejection of this design.

unresolvedItems.originalText: Procedure depends on contents of tblFormConfig
unresolvedItems.context: Static analysis of this procedure is incomplete without inspection of the actual data in tblFormConfig. The procedure is a generic dispatcher; its behavior is determined entirely by configuration data. Suggest harvester additionally extract tblFormConfig contents and treat each row as an effective code path.
unresolvedItems.suggestedNextStep: Run a separate metadata pass that extracts the full contents of tblFormConfig (FormName, FilterTemplate, OpenArgsTemplate, Callback for every row). Each row becomes an effective specification that downstream tooling can analyze individually.

diagnostics.message: Eval() of database-stored expressions: this is the worst case for static analysis and a security concern (effectively allows code injection via tblFormConfig data). Migration MUST address this; cannot be carried forward as-is.

Configuration-driven dispatch is sometimes valuable but defeats static analysis. Consider whether the dispatch flexibility is actually needed, or whether the original developer used config-driven design where simpler explicit dispatch would suffice.

SQL injection vector: sConfigKey is concatenated into SQL without parameterization. If sConfigKey is ever derived from untrusted input, this is exploitable. Migration target must use parameterized queries.
